title: Recorder
summary: An alto recorder built only from the published measurements of one real baroque alto (a Bressan recorder of the Frans Brueggen collection, as tabulated by Jan Bouterse): the bore of its three joints, the thumb hole and six finger holes, the window, the labium and step, and the windway length. The windway height is not published for this instrument and is estimated from other altos. Four fingerings of the first register are rendered as held notes at a pressure read from published register-jump thresholds, and as slow crescendos that choose no pressure at all. Speaks; not graded (no licensed reference). It speaks, but it does not sound like a recorder yet: it leaves the first register at the lowest blowing pressures, sounds higher modes of the pipe, and comes back to the first register only above 280 to 400 Pa, where a real recorder has already jumped to its second. Listening only: there is no licensed reference recording of a recorder in the library, so no spectrogram comparison is made and nothing here claims to match a real recorder.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a jet driven by a blowing pressure through the viscous windway law with the published windway length, the published window length as the jet length and the window width as the flue width, acting on a connected duct network (one jet drives the whole graph)

the published bore of the head, middle joint and foot as equal-volume cylinders, the thumb hole and six finger holes as chimney sections on ideal junctions (chimney height from the published outer diameter and the local bore), open or closed per the published fingerings, and the bore closed by the block behind the window

the window as a computed acoustic mass: the 3-D potential flow through the published 12.0 x 4.6 mm cut with parallel cheeks and the labium ramp, solved on three refinements and extrapolated at the order they show, in place of a textbook end correction; the network keeps the window's channel only as a one-sample inlet line, so no 1-D line rings across a channel whose cross modes start at 13.5 kHz
hole 7 on the foot at a derived position (24 mm below the socket rim, bracket 18 to 30 mm), open in a1, b-flat1 and b1 as the published fingerings open it

breath as the gas in the bore: exhaled breath saturated with water at 27 C with its published 4.5 % CO2 and 16.5 % O2 (dry), the woodwind breath law, read from the shared woodwind breath gas pack; it lowers every passive mode 19.1 to 19.3 cents below saturated air
fractional-delay propagation and gas-derived viscothermal loss on the long bore sections

radiation reaction and observation from the apertures themselves, so the sound is radiated pressure at a physical receiver rather than internal pressure: a compact baffled-piston load on every open hole and the open end, plus the window, which radiates from the outer face of the same 3-D solve on the head's rigid outer cylinder (resistance from the cylindrical-harmonic series, its static mass by Kramers-Kronig and taken out of the window mass, a passive chain of parallel R-L-C cells fitted from 20 Hz to 24 kHz within 1.9 %) in place of an authored window loss
deterministic oscillation: every held note sounds the same pitch and level for another jet seed, so it is a limit cycle and not a filtered seed

the start of every crescendo: each fingering begins in the first register of its pipe, at the lowest pressures. In that first-register span (the 100 ms windows within 100 cents of the first mode in the first 1.5 s, below 153 Pa) the crescendos sound f1 -23.5, a1 -37.4, b-flat1 +0.4 and b1 -1.5 cents of equal temperament on a1 = 409 Hz (median of those windows while the pressure rises), where the passive first modes are -43, -49, -7 and -8 cents
physics_missing: any reference: no licensed recording of a recorder exists in the library yet (bead pexfp.219), so these renders are listened to, not graded, and no claim of resemblance is made

register control: the loop leaves the first register at 60 to 120 Pa, far below the published first-register ceiling of a real Bressan alto (measured on an artificial mouth: F4 230, A4 305, Bb4 505, B4 490 Pa). It then sounds the pipe's second and third modes (briefly higher ones) up to about 270 Pa. Above 280 to 400 Pa it comes back to the first mode and holds it to the ramp's 600 Pa, where the real instrument has already jumped up; before the window radiation that return came only at 570 to 600 Pa, and not at all for b-flat1. So the held f1 and a1 (135 and 210 Pa) sound the pipe's second mode and are not recorder notes. The held b-flat1 and b1 (415 and 430 Pa) sound their first mode only through that return from above; before the window radiation they sounded their fourth mode. The same blowing, with the same island, reproduced a measured register ladder on the tin whistle, so the cause is in what is unknown for this windway (its height, shape and taper), not shown to be in the island

the windway: its height is not published for this alto (only its length) and is estimated from two other instruments; its curved, crescent-shaped opening, the direction of its roof, the chamfers and the taper of its section are unknown, and the recipe has a straight rectangular slit. The pressure-to-jet-speed map and every register claim depend on the height, and a sweep of the published bounds has not been made

labium offset: DERIVED, not measured. The published step and edge give the edge underside 0.27 mm on the bore side of the jet centreline at the estimated windway height, and the jet splits at the middle of the 0.25 mm face: +0.1455 mm on the pipe side (face ends +0.02 to +0.27 mm; the windway-height bounds move it from -0.225 to +0.425 mm); jet angle zero. With the gain-90 jet swinging 25 to 31 jet half-widths at the labium, this put H2 42 to 53 dB below H1 before the window radiation (36 to 70 dB across the face; the swing too was measured then). With the radiation, H2 is 58 to 75 dB below H1. So the even harmonics stay far weaker than on a measured Zen-On head: un-parity index +28 to +47 dB here (+23 to +31 before the radiation) against about -2 dB measured (Auvray et al. 2015, a comparison only)
the second and third registers: the thumb hole is a fully open or closed hole; the half-closed thumb hole that raises the register is not modelled, so only first-register fingerings are rendered

pitch: hole 7's position is derived, not measured (bracket 18 to 30 mm); the finger holes have no undercutting and no hole inertance corrections; the labium edge height is inherited from the unknown windway height (an edge at the bore or 1.25 mm above it moves every note by about +10 or -9 cents, passive); the measured bore is the tabulated maximum of a shrunken, slightly oval boxwood joint
the jet: the card is the repository's interim slot-jet card of a lattice rig, outside its Reynolds band; the displacement gain is the demonstrator value, not a measured amplification

a spectrum and attack like a real recorder: the held f1 and a1 are not first-register notes, b-flat1 and b1 reach their first register only from above (see register control), and no breath noise, chiff or edge-tone noise is modelled

the gas beyond the breath law: the CO2 fraction is the published one for exhaled breath, not measured in a played recorder; no temperature gradient along the bore, and the published pitch was measured in rooms at 15 to 27 C (about 40 cents between them)
native verification beyond one fingering at two mechanics clocks and two jet seeds on a few files
